trial_court: Court of Sh. Gaurav Sharma, JSCC-Cum-ASCJ-Cum-Guardian Judge, East Karkardooma Courts/Delhi, Civ Suit No. 296/2020

parties.respondent_defendant: Ms. Sonia Talwar, defendants; Ms. Vishali Talwar, defendant no.2; Ms. Rupali Talwar, defendant no.3

facts_of_case: Plaintiff Karan Singh claimed exclusive ownership of property; defendants Sonia Talwar and her daughters Vishali and Rupali were licensees who lost their right to reside after Sher Singh's death.

legal_principles.principle: A Will can confer ownership on account of devolution after the death of the testator.
legal_principles.held: In view of the same, when Vishnu Devi did pass away subsequent to executing the documents that she did, which included the Will document, the ownership of the suit property did pass on to Sajjan Singh.

legal_principles.principle: The requirement of a Will having to be proved by summoning an attesting witness is not applicable where the disputes are not classical disputes between legal heirs.
legal_principles.held: Such an argument also does not convince the Court. The requirement of a Will having to be proved by summoning of an attesting witness is an argument that can be put forth in cases where there are inter se disputes between the legal heirs of a deceased testator and the validity of the Will is questioned.

outcome.final_order: The plaintiff's evidence was taken as credible, and the defendants' failure to produce evidence led to the decree in favor of the plaintiff.

keywords: Mere assertions cannot take place of proof
use_for_drafting: preparing for a property dispute hearing
